name: What older-home problems should be inspected before planning a remodel?

mainEntity.name: What hidden issues should be checked first in an older Los Angeles home before spending money on design and finishes?
mainEntity.text: What hidden issues should be checked first in an older Los Angeles home before spending money on design and finishes?

acceptedAnswer.text: The first inspection pass should focus on systems and structure, not finishes. In older Los Angeles-area homes, the biggest unknowns are usually foundation condition, crawl-space framing, roof leaks, sewer or drain line deterioration, outdated electrical panels, undersized wiring, and hidden plumbing failures. Moisture damage is especially important because it often spreads behind walls and under floors before it becomes visible. If the house was built before modern earthquake standards, check for bolting, cripple-wall bracing, chimney stability, and other seismic vulnerabilities. Homes built before 1978 may also require special care for lead-based paint during repair work. A good modernization plan starts with a diagnostic phase so the team can sequence repairs correctly. That usually means opening the right areas first, fixing infrastructure, then designing finishes around what the home actually needs. It is cheaper to learn about a failing sewer line or a weak panel before selecting cabinetry, tile, or custom millwork.
acceptedAnswer.description: Before design work starts, inspect the foundation, framing, roof, plumbing, electrical system, drainage, and signs of moisture damage. Older homes may also need checks for seismic bracing, unreinforced masonry, lead paint, and outdated wiring or panels. Fixing these issues early prevents expensive redesigns after walls are opened.
